_note: Entirely synthetic. Names, studies, figures and quotes are invented for the demo; none are real BPI data.

studies.title: SME Online Loan Application Drop-off Survey 2026
studies.summary: Online and phone survey of SME owners in Metro Manila who started an online loan application in the past 12 months, measuring why they did not finish.

findings.text: Documentation requirements were the most-cited reason SME owners abandoned an online loan application (46%).
Not knowing how long approval would take was the second most-cited reason for dropping off (40%).
Fees ranked third of seven drop-off reasons, cited by 38% of owners who started an online loan application.
Among owners aged 20-29, 44% cited fees as a reason for dropping off.
Among owners aged 30-40, 33% cited fees as a reason for dropping off.
App errors during document upload were cited by 22% of owners who dropped off.

studies.title: Nationwide SME Banking Needs Study 2025
studies.summary: Nationwide face-to-face and online survey of SME owners on financing needs, including why online loan applications are left unfinished.

findings.text: Documentation requirements were the top reason SME owners stopped an online loan application (52%).
Unclear approval time was the second reason owners dropped off (44%).
Collateral requirements ranked third among reasons for abandoning a loan application (31%).
Fees were not among the top barriers: 12% of SME owners cited them, sixth of seven drop-off reasons.

studies.title: Visayas SME Owner Focus Groups 2025
studies.summary: Six focus groups with SME owners in Cebu and Iloilo on their experience of applying for business loans online.

findings.text: In the Cebu and Iloilo groups, participants described fees as a minor concern in a loan application; what they raised instead was not knowing whom to call when an application stalled.
Participants described wanting a named contact person who can answer questions while a loan application is in progress.
Participants described re-uploading documents they had already submitted as the point where they gave up on an online loan application.
The fees are fine as long as they're clear. What I need is someone I can call when the application gets stuck.
Okay lang ang fees, basta may makakausap ako kapag may problema. (The fees are okay, as long as I have someone to talk to when there's a problem.)
I'd rather talk to one person who knows my business than fill in the same form three times.
When the app asked for my ITR again, I just went to the branch instead.

studies.title: SME Loan Journey Benchmark 2022
studies.summary: Nationwide benchmark survey of SME owners' loan application journeys across banks.

findings.text: In 2022, documentation requirements led the reasons SME owners abandoned a loan application (41%).
In 2022, fees were the second most-cited reason for abandoning a loan application (35%).

studies.title: Card Rewards Preference Pulse Q1 2026
studies.summary: Online pulse survey of young professionals in Metro Manila on preferred credit card rewards.

findings.text: Cashback was the preferred credit card reward for 54% of young professionals.
Travel rewards were the preferred credit card reward for 19% of young professionals.

studies.title: Credit Card Value Proposition Test 2026
studies.summary: Online survey testing credit card reward propositions with young professionals in Metro Manila.

findings.text: Only 21% of young professionals chose cashback as their preferred credit card reward.
Travel rewards were the first choice of credit card reward for 47% of young professionals.

studies.title: Market Vendor QR Payments Groups 2026
studies.summary: Four focus groups with public market vendors in Davao City and Cagayan de Oro on accepting QR payments.

findings.text: In the Davao and Cagayan de Oro groups, participants described QR payments as convenient for small amounts but worried about confirming that a payment had arrived before handing over goods.
Participants described keeping cash as their default because their own suppliers still ask to be paid in cash.
With QR I have to check my phone before I hand over the fish, and when it's busy that slows me down.
My suppliers want cash, so the QR money just sits in the app until I withdraw it.

studies.title: Card Application Panel 2026
studies.summary: Online panel survey of 1,200 credit card applicants aged 20-40 in Metro Manila who started a credit card application in the card app but did not finish it in the past six months.

findings.text: Verifying their ID with a selfie was the top reason applicants aged 20-40 did not finish a card application (48%).
For 37% of applicants aged 20-40, the annual fee was a reason they did not finish a card application.
Among applicants aged 20-27, 55% cited ID verification.
Among applicants aged 28-40, 41% cited ID verification.
Selfie-step errors were cited by 14% of applicants.

studies.title: Credit Card Applicant Study 2025: Ages 41-60
studies.summary: Nationwide face-to-face and online survey of 900 credit card applicants aged 41-60 on why they did not finish a card application.

findings.text: ID verification was a leading reason applicants aged 41-60 did not finish a card application (39%).
Applicants aged 41-60 rarely named the annual fee: 11% said it was a reason they did not finish a card application, sixth of seven reasons.

studies.title: Visayas Card Applicant Focus Groups 2026
studies.summary: Six focus groups with young credit card applicants in Cebu City and Iloilo City who started a card application in the app, on where and why they did not finish.

findings.text: In the Cebu and Iloilo groups, participants described the ID and selfie check failing again and again as the point where they walked away from their card application.
Participants described one-time PIN texts arriving late or not at all, so the page expired before they could finish.
Participants described the annual fee as acceptable if approval came quickly; the fee was rarely why they left a card application unfinished.
Tatlong beses na akong nag-selfie, ayaw pa rin tanggapin. Nakakainis talaga. (I took a selfie three times and it still would not accept it. Really annoying.)
I wasn't sure which ID they wanted, my school ID or my postal ID. I got confused and stopped.
I didn't want to send a photo of my ID to an app I wasn't sure was really the bank's.
The PIN came after the page expired, three times in a row. It felt like they weren't taking me seriously.
When I switched to my passport the selfie check finally worked. What a relief.
The annual fee doesn't bother me as long as they approve the card quickly.

studies.title: Davao Young Earners Card Interviews 2025
studies.summary: Twenty in-depth interviews with young earners in Davao City about applying for their first credit card in a card app.

findings.text: Participants described being asked for a second valid ID they did not have as the reason they did not finish a card application.
Wala akong passport o driver's license, so hindi ko alam kung paano ituloy. (I don't have a passport or driver's license, so I didn't know how to continue.)

studies.title: Mobile App Experience Tracker 2025-2026
studies.summary: Two-wave tracking survey of 2,000 mobile banking app users nationwide per wave (wave 1 November 2025, wave 2 June 2026) on satisfaction with the app.

findings.text: Among users aged 18-34, satisfaction with the mobile app rose from 61% in wave 1 to 72% in wave 2.
Among users aged 50-65, satisfaction with the mobile app fell from 66% in wave 1 to 54% in wave 2; slower log-in after the redesign was their most-cited complaint.
Across all users, satisfaction with the mobile app was 64% in wave 2, unchanged from wave 1.

studies.title: ATM Access Survey 2026
studies.summary: Nationwide survey of 1,600 retail banking customers on ATM access, with results for Metro Manila, Luzon outside NCR, Visayas and Mindanao, and for urban and rural barangays.

findings.text: In Metro Manila, 57% said long lines at ATMs were a problem.
In Luzon outside NCR, 24% said long lines at ATMs were a problem.
In Visayas, 19% said long lines at ATMs were a problem.
In Mindanao, 17% said long lines at ATMs were a problem.
In rural barangays, 41% of customers said the nearest ATM is too far away.
In urban barangays, 9% of customers said the nearest ATM is too far away.

studies.title: Bank Impersonation Text Survey 2026
studies.summary: Nationwide survey of 1,800 retail banking customers on text messages that pretend to be from a bank, clicking their links and reporting them.

findings.text: 52% received at least one text message pretending to be from a bank in the past three months.
7% said they had clicked a link in such a message.
Among customers aged 55-65, 13% had clicked a link in such a message.
Among customers aged 18-24, 4% had clicked a link in such a message.
61% did not know how to report a fake bank message.

studies.title: Bank Impersonation Text Survey 2022
studies.summary: 2022 wave of the survey on fake bank text messages, with 1,200 retail banking customers nationwide.

findings.text: In 2022, 31% received at least one text message pretending to be from a bank in the past three months.
In 2022, 11% said they had clicked a link in such a message.
In 2022, 72% did not know how to report a fake bank message.

studies.title: Scam Victim Focus Groups 2025
studies.summary: Four focus groups with people who lost money to a caller or message pretending to be from a bank.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through a fraud-support hotline and screened for people who had lost money to a caller or message pretending to be from a bank in the past year.

population.segment: People who lost money to bank impersonation scams

findings.text: Participants described the scam call creating panic about a blocked account, which pushed them to act before checking.
In the NCR, Cavite, Iloilo and Davao groups, participants described telling no one for days because they felt foolish.
He knew my name and my last transaction. Paano ko hindi paniniwalaan? (How could I not believe him?)
I only told my daughter a week later.

studies.title: Contact Center Experience Survey 2026
studies.summary: Post-call survey of 1,000 customers on first-call resolution and hold times at the contact center.

population.segment: Customers who called the contact center

findings.text: 46% had their issue resolved in the first call.
Among callers aged 60-70, 28% had their issue resolved in the first call.
39% held for more than 10 minutes before speaking to an agent.

studies.title: Complaint Handling Focus Groups 2024
studies.summary: Four focus groups with customers who filed a complaint, on how their cases were handled and closed.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited, with consent, from customers who had filed a complaint in the previous six months.

findings.text: Participants described having to explain their problem again to each new agent as the point at which they considered closing their account.
In the NCR, Cebu and Cagayan de Oro groups, participants described never being told that a case had been closed.
Tatlong beses ko nang ikinuwento. (I've told the story three times already.)
They closed the ticket. Nobody told me.

studies.title: Financial Literacy Baseline Survey 2024
studies.summary: Nationwide baseline of basic money knowledge among 2,000 adults, and how much practical help they want.

findings.text: 34% correctly answered a simple compound interest question.
Among adults aged 18-24, 39% answered the compound interest question correctly.
Among adults aged 55-65, 25% answered the compound interest question correctly.
61% wanted more practical money lessons from their bank.

studies.title: Money Skills Workshop Evaluation 2026
studies.summary: Survey of 640 attendees in two waves, before and after a money skills workshop, plus 18 in-depth interviews.

findings.text: Among attendees aged 18-29, correct answers to the compound interest question rose from 38% before the workshop to 61% after.
Among attendees aged 50-65, correct answers rose only from 27% before the workshop to 29% after.
In the interviews, participants described worked examples using their own payslip as what made the lessons stick.
When she used my own payslip, I finally saw where the money goes.

studies.title: Typhoon and Household Finances Survey 2023
studies.summary: Survey of 1,200 households in typhoon-prone areas of the Visayas and Mindanao on income losses and money set aside for emergencies.

findings.text: 62% had lost income to a typhoon or flood in the past three years.
In Eastern Visayas, 74% had lost income to a typhoon or flood.
14% had money set aside that would last a month after a disaster.

studies.title: Typhoon Recovery Focus Groups: Eastern Visayas 2025
studies.summary: Four focus groups in Tacloban and Leyte with households rebuilding after a typhoon, on how they raised money.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through barangay offices in areas hit by a typhoon in the previous year.

findings.text: In the Tacloban and Leyte groups, participants described selling livestock and pawning jewellery as the first ways to raise money after the storm.
Participants described relatives working abroad and in Manila as the help that arrived fastest after the storm.
Naibenta namin ang baboy para may pambili ng yero. (We sold the pig so we could buy roofing sheets.)
My brother in Manila sent money before the government aid came.

studies.title: Gig and Delivery Workers Income Survey 2025
studies.summary: Survey of 900 delivery, ride-hailing and online freelance workers on how much their income moves from week to week.

population.segment: Delivery, ride-hailing and online freelance workers

findings.text: 55% said their weekly income changed by more than a quarter from one week to the next.
Among delivery and ride-hailing workers, 64% had income that swung this much.
Among online freelancers, 41% had income that swung this much.
Only 12% had money set aside to cover a bad month.

studies.title: Delivery Rider Income Focus Groups 2026
studies.summary: Four focus groups with delivery and ride-hailing workers in Metro Manila and Cebu on uneven income and cashing out.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through rider community groups and screened for at least six months of active riding.

findings.text: In the NCR and Cebu groups, participants described good weeks and bad weeks as unpredictable and used good weeks to cover bad ones.
Participants described cashing out their earnings every day because waiting felt risky.
Araw-araw ako nagca-cash out. Baka bukas wala na. (I cash out every day. Tomorrow it might be gone.)
Rainy days are good for orders, bad for my motorbike.

studies.title: Fisherfolk Household Finances Focus Groups 2026
studies.summary: Five focus groups with fisherfolk households in Zamboanga, General Santos and Bohol on lean months and boat owners.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through fisherfolk associations in coastal barangays.

findings.text: In the Zamboanga, General Santos and Bohol groups, participants described lean months when the catch falls and advances from boat owners fill the gap.
Participants described repaying boat owners with part of each catch, which tied them to selling at the boat owner's price.
Kapag habagat, walang huli, kaya utang muna. (In the monsoon season there is no catch, so we run up a debt first.)
The boat owner gives us an advance, so we sell to him.

studies.title: Rooftop Solar Interest Survey 2025
studies.summary: Survey of 850 homeowners in Luzon on installing rooftop solar if they could pay in instalments.

findings.text: 46% of homeowners would install rooftop solar if they could pay for it in instalments.
In NCR, 41% would install rooftop solar with instalments.
In Central Luzon, 54% would install rooftop solar with instalments.
Upfront cost held back 71% of interested homeowners.

studies.title: Green Products Attitudes Focus Groups 2026
studies.summary: Four focus groups with working adults in Metro Manila and Cebu on green banking products and proof of impact.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through an online panel and screened for an interest in environmental causes.

findings.text: In the NCR and Cebu groups, participants described supporting green causes but balked at paying more for a green product without proof of impact.
Participants described wanting to see which projects their money funded before trusting a green label.
Show me the trees, not the logo.
Green is nice, pero mahal ang bilihin. (Green is nice, but everything is expensive.)

studies.title: Customers with Disabilities Focus Groups 2026
studies.summary: Four focus groups with customers who have visual or mobility disabilities, on branches and the bank's website.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through disability organisations; sessions were held in accessible venues with sign-language interpretation.

population.segment: Customers with visual or mobility disabilities

findings.text: Participants described ramps that led to locked side doors and counters placed too high to use from a wheelchair.
In the NCR and Cebu groups, participants described buttons on the bank's website without labels, which screen readers announce only as button.
The ramp is there, but the door at the end is locked.
My screen reader says button, button, button.

subgroup.segment: Call center agent with low vision, 29

studies.title: Data Sharing Comfort Tracker 2025-2026
studies.summary: Two-wave tracking survey of 1,500 retail banking customers nationwide per wave (wave 1 October 2025, wave 2 April 2026) on the bank using their data for offers.

findings.text: Among customers aged 21-34, comfort with the bank using their transaction history to tailor offers rose from 52% in wave 1 to 61% in wave 2.
Among customers aged 45-60, comfort fell from 41% in wave 1 to 33% in wave 2, after a data breach at another company was in the news.
Across all customers, 48% were comfortable in wave 2, up from 46% in wave 1.
44% said they would rather get offers based on how they bank than generic ones.
71% wanted a simple switch to turn off data use for offers.

studies.title: Provincial Customers Data Sharing Pulse 2025
studies.summary: Pulse survey of 600 customers aged 45-70 in the Visayas and Mindanao on how they want their data used.

findings.text: 12% of customers aged 45-70 in the Visayas and Mindanao said they would rather get offers based on how they bank than generic ones.
58% said they would want to be asked each time before their data is used.

studies.title: Payday Budget Focus Groups 2025
studies.summary: Three focus groups with entry-level workers in Metro Manila, Cavite and Pampanga on making their pay last.
studies.recruitment: Participants were recruited through workplace partners and screened for monthly pay at or near the minimum wage.

findings.text: Participants described their pay being spoken for before it arrives, with rent, debts and family support taking the first share.
In the NCR, Cavite and Pampanga groups, participants described keeping coins and small change aside as the only way of holding money back that felt possible.
Sweldo today, wala na bukas. (Payday today, gone tomorrow.)
I keep a jar for coins. That's what I can put aside.

studies.title: Workplace Money Wellness Programme Evaluation 2025
studies.summary: Survey of 520 employees of payroll client companies before and after a money wellness programme, plus 16 in-depth interviews.

findings.text: The share of employees who ran out of money before payday fell from 48% before the programme to 36% after.
Among employees aged 22-29, the share who ran out of money before payday fell from 55% to 37%.
In the interviews, participants described the salary advance as the part they valued and the budgeting sessions as useful but hard to attend during shifts.
I don't go to the five-six collector any more; the advance comes from payroll.

studies.title: Corporate Treasury Online Banking Survey 2024
studies.summary: Survey of 320 corporate treasury staff in Metro Manila and Cebu on bulk transfers and sign-off in the online banking portal.

findings.text: 58% of treasury teams used bulk transfer files for payroll each month.
41% said multi-level sign-off in the online portal slowed urgent supplier releases.
Among treasury teams in Cebu, 49% said multi-level sign-off slowed urgent releases.
